reason: All 6 hidden tests error because they instantiate \core\check\security\securitymessages and read report_security strings check_securitymessages_action_lock/_enable/_enableandlock/_notification_disabled, while the agent named its check newloginnotifications with its own strings; neither name is given in the issue. The agent's check does distinguish disabled / not-locked / forced states and the messages.php default is MESSAGE_FORCED (locked+enabled per translate_message_default_setting), so the issue's behaviour is produced. One minor divergence (agent warns when no processor is enabled, test_disabled_processor_is_ignored expects OK) is an unspecified design choice, and the per-processor 'Lock'/'Enable' detail text is a presentation choice the issue does not ask for.

49 of 52 hidden tests error on undefined methods: the tests use create_client(), get_client(), create_secret(int clientid), get_secrets(), revoke_secret(), add_redirect_uri(int, uri), remove_redirect_uri(int, uri), update_client(int, array) and validate_redirect_uri(identifier, uri) returning client_entity objects, whereas the agent exposed get_client_by_identifier(), generate_client_secret(string identifier), get_client_secrets(), revoke_client_secret(), create_redirect_uri(), remove_redirect_uri(int id), update_client(int, string, ?string) and a format-only validate_redirect_uri(uri), none of which the issue names. The agent's revoke cascade, reactivate semantics, delete-requires-revoked, per-client 2-secret limit and HTTPS/loopback validation match the clarifications. Reservation: the agent's validate_redirect_uri never checks a candidate against the client's registered URIs (the 'exact match' rule), and create_secret does not refuse public/revoked clients, but the issue does not spell those out.

The issue asks for exactly one thing, the missing continue after the 'not an analysable question' debugging() call, and the agent added exactly that; the first hidden test (test_get_cached_skips_stale_slot_row) passes with 3 assertions. The second test, test_get_cached_skips_orphan_variant_row, inserts a subquestion variant row with no parent entry and expects a debugging() call and no fatal error, which requires the extra guard the developers added in the subquestion/variant branch (assigning to $this->subquestionstats[$id]->variantstats on a missing key errors). That hardening is not mentioned in the issue text, so the agent's narrower reading is reasonable; the tests encode the developers' broader scope.

The only failing assertion is assertStringContainsString('relativepath', serialize($lo)) / assertStringNotContainsString('fullpath', ...) in test_file_logger_relative_path: the developers added a new $relativepath property and serialise it, while the agent keeps the bare filename inside the existing $fullpath property and resolves it via get_fullpath(). The agent's logger accepts a bare filename, creates the file under backuptempdir, serialises only the filename, rebuilds the path on __wakeup against the current $CFG->backuptempdir and still handles legacy absolute paths, which is what the issue asks; backup_factory is switched to pass $backupid.'.log' as well. The failure is purely the property name chosen for serialisation.

The agent enables $builder->useAttributes(true), which is the behaviour the issue asks for (attribute-based injection, injectOn on existing instances). The hidden tests fail on \core\di::make(), a new static convenience method the developers added and the issue never mentions: di_test::test_attribute_injection_enabled and test_make_with_params call di::make() (2 errors), and task_log_test calls \core\di::make($classname) (1 error). test_attribute_injection_enabled also depends on the fixture \core\tests\di\example_class which was not copied. With the agent's container, injection of #[Inject] properties works (its own tests use get() and injectOn).

Two hidden tests fail for behavioural reasons. password_test::test_update_keeps_password_reset_tokens_on_rehash_only: the agent put delete_records('user_password_resets') inside the if ($passwordchanged || $algorithmchanged) block, so a rehash-only update (same password, legacy hash upgraded on normal login) wipes a pending reset token even though the password did not change, contrary to 'invalidate ... if the password is changed'; the developers guard it with if ($passwordchanged). imsenterprise_test::test_user_update_email_invalidates_password_reset_tokens: the IMS Enterprise import updates the email with a direct $DB->update_record('user'), bypassing core_user::update_user, so the agent's hook misses that email-change path which the issue explicitly asks to look for ('any other similar ... that may need similar treatment'). The user_test and login_lib_test parts pass.
